Everything needed to build, extend and run a site on {DevelopersOnly}: a hybrid-headless WordPress theme where PHP owns the CMS and a custom REST API, and a React application renders every front-end page.

Each tab below covers one area. Start with Getting started for the architecture and a first-run checklist.
How the theme is put together, and what to do on a fresh install.

[{"nav_label": "Overview", "title": "Overview", "media": "", "copy": "Orientation

The theme splits cleanly in two. WordPress remains the system of record: it stores content, renders the admin, and serves a REST API. It does not render the front end. Instead, every request returns a minimal HTML document containing SEO meta, structured data and an empty <div id="root">. React mounts there and handles all routing and rendering from that point on.

This gives you the editorial experience of WordPress with the interaction model of a single-page app, and it keeps SEO intact because the crawler-critical tags are still rendered server-side by header.php before React boots.

The three ideas worth internalising

No ACF
Every custom field is declared in PHP, as a subclass of the abstract DO_Custom_Post_Type. Fields are code, versioned in git, and identical across environments. There is no field configuration stored in the database to sync.
Panels
A landing page is an ordered list of panels. Each panel has a type (blocks, quotes, stats…), and the type determines which fields the editor sees in wp-admin and which React component renders on the front end. Adding a page layout means adding a panel, not a template.
Extensions
Site-specific work lives in extensions/ and is auto-discovered. Adding a post type, panel, template, REST route or stylesheet requires dropping a correctly-named file into place — no core file is edited, so the framework stays upgradeable.

Drop the theme into wp-content/themes/developers-only and activate it. Before it will load at all, one constant must be defined.

The DO_ENVIRONMENT constant

Required

The theme reads DO_ENVIRONMENT on the very first line of functions.php. If it is not defined before the theme loads, PHP will fatal. Define it in wp-config.php, above the ABSPATH block.

php · wp-config.php 
// One of: 'local', 'dev', 'stg', 'prod'
define( 'DO_ENVIRONMENT', 'local' );

The value drives a surprising amount of behaviour, so it is worth getting right per environment:

ValueAsset cache-bustingAdmin colourIndexingAnalytics
localtime() — never cachedEctoplasmAllowedOff
devDeploy stampOceannoindex forcedOff
stgDeploy stampLightnoindex forcedOff
prodDeploy stampMidnightPer-postGTM, on consent

The instantly-recognisable admin colour scheme per environment is deliberate: it makes it hard to edit production content while believing you are on staging. The picker is removed from user profiles so it cannot be overridden.

First-run checklist

  1. Define DO_ENVIRONMENT in wp-config.php.
  2. Activate the theme. Post types register on init; menus and image sizes register on after_setup_theme.
  3. Visit Settings → Permalinks and save once, to flush rewrite rules.
  4. Run npm install then npm run build so public/dist/ exists — the theme enqueues nothing until the Vite manifest is present.
  5. Create a Landing Page with the slug home. The React router maps / to that post specifically.
  6. Populate Appearance → Menus for the four registered locations.
  7. Fill in Appearance → Site Settings (cookie consent text, header/footer scripts).
Why the home page is special

index.tsx routes / to <Layout postType="landing-page" slug="home" />. A landing page whose slug is home also gets its permalink rewritten to / by devo_api_custom_data(), and its title forced to “Home” on save. Without that post, the site root renders nothing.

Vite entry points

Five entries are compiled into public/dist/. CSS filenames are lowercased and unhashed so PHP can enqueue them by a stable name; JavaScript is content-hashed and resolved through the manifest.

EntrySourceOutputEnqueued
indexapp/index.tsxhashed .js + index.cssEvery front-end page, as type="module"
devo-globalapp/styles/devo-global.scssdevo-global.cssEvery front-end page
extensions-globalextensions/app/styles/extensions-global.scssextensions-global.cssEvery front-end page, after devo-global

Known mismatch

functions.php enqueues the login stylesheet as public/dist/devo-login.css, but Vite emits login.css. The login screen currently loads a 404. Fix by changing either the entry name in vite.config.ts or the path in devo_login_stylesheet().

Why the script tag has no ?ver=

The React entry is enqueued with $ver = null. This is load-bearing, not an oversight. Lazily-imported chunks reference the entry by its bare hashed filename; adding a ?ver= query would cause the browser to fetch and evaluate the module a second time under a different URL, mounting a second React root and crashing the app. The content hash in the filename already handles cache busting.

php · functions.php 
wp_enqueue_script( 'react-index', /* … */ $index_file->file, [], null, TRUE );

A companion filter, devo_js_module(), rewrites that tag to type="module" on output, handling both the pre- and post-WordPress 6.3 tag formats.

Path alias

@ resolves to app/ in both vite.config.ts and the tsconfigs. Extension files are imported by absolute path from the project root (/extensions/...) because they sit outside the alias.

A cold page load runs through PHP once, then never again — subsequent navigation is client-side, and only data crosses the wire.

  1. WordPress routesRewrite rules resolve the URL to a post. index.php renders the shell.
  2. header.phpEmits title, canonical, Open Graph tags and JSON-LD from the post's SEO field mapping.
  3. Assets enqueuedevo_scripts() reads the Vite manifest and enqueues the module bundle plus global CSS.
  4. React mountsindex.tsx mounts into #root; the router basename comes from window.relativeHomeURL.
  5. Data fetchTemplateLoader calls the REST API for the post, picks a template, and renders.

PHP globals handed to JavaScript

Options can hold secrets, so there is deliberately no get_option() proxy route. Anything the front end needs is injected as a global by devo_js_globals(), on both wp_head and admin_head.

GlobalSourceUsed for
window.devoEnvDO_ENVIRONMENTGates API endpoint logging to non-production
window.homeURLhome_url()Base for the REST endpoint in globalVariables.ts
window.relativeHomeURLhome_url('', 'relative')React Router basename — supports subdirectory installs
window.devoGTMDO_GTM_IDContainer ID injected on consent
window.devoCookieConsentTextSite SettingsConsent banner copy, editable without a deploy
window.menus—Initialised empty; the menu store populates it as a request-level cache

WordPress cleanup

functions.php strips a considerable amount of core output that a headless front end has no use for: the block library and global styles stylesheets, wp-embed, emoji detection, RSD/WLW links, feed links, oEmbed discovery, the generator tag, shortlinks, core sitemaps, and the REST link header. Rewrite rules for authors, categories, tags, attachments, comments, feeds, embeds and trackbacks are removed too, along with the Posts and Pages admin menus (Pages is relocated under Settings).

Custom post types, fields, and everything that appears in wp-admin.

[{"nav_label": "Post types", "title": "Custom post types", "media": "", "copy": "PHP layer PHP

Every post type is a singleton subclass of the abstract DO_Custom_Post_Type (api/classes/class-custom-post-type.php). The base class registers the post type, builds the wp-admin meta boxes, validates and saves the fields, mirrors selected values into native post_* columns, and exposes typed field output on the REST API — all from five declarative methods.

Where content actually lives

Content is not stored in post_content. It lives in post meta. The class mirrors chosen meta fields into post_title, post_content, post_excerpt, post_name and the featured image on save, so WordPress search, the admin list table and permalinks keep working normally.

The five methods

MethodReturnsPurpose
post_type()stringThe raw slug, e.g. devo_blog. The last underscore-separated segment becomes the meta prefix.
post_type_args()arrayRaw args merged into register_post_type(). Usually empty.
settings()arrayTheme-specific configuration — column mirroring, SEO, schema, slug, admin placement.
meta_fields()array[ 'Box Name' => [ 'Field Label' => 'field_type' ] ]. Defines both the admin UI and the REST output.
admin_fields()arrayColumns shown in the admin list table. Field labels, or the literals title, post_date, author.

Copy api/classes/post-types/NEW_POST_TYPE_TEMPLATE.php to start — it carries an annotated version of all five methods with a worked example.

php · a minimal post type 
class DO_Case_Study extends DO_Custom_Post_Type {

    protected function post_type(): string {
        return 'devo_case_study';   // meta prefix → 'study'
    }

    protected function post_type_args(): array { return []; }

    protected function settings(): array {
        return [
            'post_title'     => 'Title',
            'post_name'      => 'Title',
            'post_thumbnail' => 'SEO Image||Image',
            'post_excerpt'   => 'Description',
            'slug'           => 'case-studies',
            'has_archive'    => TRUE,
            'hide_field'     => 'Hidden',
            'seo' => [
                'title'       => 'Title',
                'image'       => 'SEO Image||Image',
                'description' => 'Description',
            ],
            'schema' => [
                '@type'    => 'Article',
                'headline' => 'Title',
                'image'    => 'Image',
            ],
        ];
    }

    protected function meta_fields(): array {
        return [
            'Case Study' => [
                'Title'       => 'text',
                'Image'       => 'media',
                'SEO Image'   => 'media',
                'Description' => 'html',
                'Content'     => 'wp_editor',
                'Hidden'      => 'binary',
            ],
        ];
    }

    protected function admin_fields(): array {
        return [ 'Title', 'Hidden', 'post_date' ];
    }
}
$devo_case_study = DO_Case_Study::get_instance();

Meta key convention

You never write meta keys by hand. They are derived from the field label:

Key derivation 
{meta_prefix}_{snake_case_label}[_{suffix}]

devo_landing_page  →  prefix "page"
  "SEO Title"      →  page_seo_title
  "Title"    (panel 3)  →  page_title_3
  "Panel Type" (panel 3)  →  page_panel_type_3

Both sides of the stack implement the same transform, and they must stay in sync: devo_meta_field_key() in api/functions.helpers.php, and metaFieldKey() in app/utils/helpers/. The prefix defaults to the last segment of the post type slug and can be overridden with the meta_prefix setting.

Dynamic interfaces — how panels are built

The dynamic_interface setting turns a single meta box definition into N repeating boxes whose fields change based on a type selector. This is the mechanism behind both landing-page panels and the form builder.

php · class-landing-page.php 
'dynamic_interface' => [
    'settings' => [
        'type'                         => 'array',
        'nested'                       => 'Panel Type',
        'default_meta_boxes'          => [ 'Hero', 'SEO', 'Admin' ],
        'dynamic_meta_box'            => 'Panel',
        'dynamic_meta_box_title_field' => 'Title',
    ],
    'field_configuration' => [
        'Panel Type' => $this->panel_fields(),
    ],
],

Reading that in order:

  • 'type' => 'array' creates a counter field named after the box — Panel becomes page_panel_count — and repeats the box that many times as “Panel 1”, “Panel 2”…, suffixing every field key with _1, _2…
  • 'nested' => 'Panel Type' makes the Panel Type select drive the box's contents: whichever value is chosen, the matching entry from field_configuration is merged in. Choosing Quotes reveals the quotes repeater; choosing Stats reveals the stats fields.
  • default_meta_boxes are the fixed boxes that always render (Hero, SEO, Admin).

On the React side LandingPage.tsx reads page_panel_count, loops that many times, and hands each index to <Panel>, which reads page_panel_type_{N} to pick a component. The counter is the entire contract between the two halves.

The icon library

DO_Icon does something worth knowing about: on save it rewrites the uploaded SVG, replacing every black fill and stroke with currentColor and adding fill="currentColor" to the root <svg> if absent. Icons therefore inherit text colour wherever they are placed. It also flags the attachment with an icon meta key, which is what DO_Media_Library_Filter_Tab uses to give the Media Library an Icons tab.

Options screens

DO_Options_Screen creates a settings page with the same field vocabulary as post types. Values are stored as a single option per field group, named {screen_name}_{group}.

php · functions.php, devo_create_objects() 
$site_settings = new DO_Options_Screen( 'site_settings' );
$site_settings->settings( [
    'submenu'    => 'themes.php',
    'page_title' => 'Site Settings',

    'Cookie Consent Text' => 'html',

Forms are content, not code. An editor builds one in wp-admin under Forms; the front end fetches its definition and renders it generically.

  1. DefineEditor adds fields to a devo_form post. Field type drives which extra settings appear.
  2. FetchReact calls /devo-form/?formID=; DO_Form_Builder::display() returns the field tree.
  3. RenderRenderForm walks the tree, FormFieldLoader maps each type to a component.
  4. SubmitPOST to /devo-form-submit/ as urlencoded. Every value is sanitised by type.
  5. RespondSubmission stored, alert and confirmation emails sent, form returned with errors or a thank-you.

Validation and error reporting

Validation is server-side and authoritative. Required fields that arrive empty are collected into missing_fields and the response carries error: true with the form intact, so React can re-render it with the offending fields marked and the good values preserved. Nothing is stored when validation fails.

Email routing

Two notification paths exist, chosen automatically:

  • Conditional — if Email Submissions Logic is configured, the value of a nominated field selects the recipient list. A “Which department?” select can route to different inboxes.
  • Simple — otherwise, the comma-separated Email Submissions To list receives everything.

A confirmation email goes to the submitter if confirmation content is configured and a field whose name contains email was submitted. Mail goes out through DO_Send_Simple_Email, a thin wrapper over wp_mail() that overrides the from address and name, and reports a status code and log back into the API response.

Per-form callbacks

After a successful submission the handler fires a dynamic action, letting you attach bespoke behaviour to one form without touching the handler:

php · in an extensions/api/*.php file 
add_action( 'devo_form_submit_newsletter_signup', function( $fields ) {
    // $fields is keyed by field name; each value carries
    // 'label', 'field_type' and 'current_value'.
} );

Front-end field components

FormFieldLoader maps a field type to a component. Available: alphabet, binary, button, checkbox, email, hidden, phone, privacy_policy, search, select, select_list, text, textarea. An unmapped type renders nothing rather than erroring.

Search is a panel, not a page, and it is configured entirely per-instance. Three classes collaborate:

DO_Search
Registers GET /devo-search, reads the panel's configuration out of post meta, and orchestrates the other two.
DO_Search_Query
Turns the merged default and user query into a WP_Query, returning posts, total count, page count and current page.
DO_Search_UI
Builds the filter controls with their currently available options, the results statement, and the sort options — so the front end never hard-codes a filter.

The endpoint is told which panel to read via postID, metaPrefix and metaSuffix; everything else in the query string is treated as a filter. That means the same route serves every search panel on the site with no route-level configuration.

http 
GET /wp-json/wp/v2/devo-search
      ?postID=42&metaPrefix=page&metaSuffix=_3
      &s=climate&paged=2&sort=date_desc&subject=policy,research

Reserved parameters are posts_per_page, paged, s, sort, postID, metaPrefix, metaSuffix. Anything else is matched against the panel's configured Search Fields and mapped to its meta key. Default sort is date_desc; built-in options are publish date, A–Z and Z–A unless the panel defines a custom sort list.

The response merges query and UI:

json · response shape 
{
  "posts": [ … ],            // full enriched post objects
  "found_posts": 137,
  "pages": 9,
  "current_page": 2,
  "ui": { … },               // resolved filter controls + options
  "results_statement": "…",
  "sort": { … }
}

Response enrichment

Every post response passes through devo_api_custom_data(), which adds the properties React actually consumes:

PropertyContents

Routing

Three routes cover the whole site. The basename comes from window.relativeHomeURL, so subdirectory installs work without configuration.

tsx · app/index.tsx 
<BrowserRouter basename={ window.relativeHomeURL || undefined }>
  <Routes>
    <Route path="/"                element={ <Layout postType="landing-page" slug="home" /> } />
    <Route path="/:postType/:slug" element={ <Layout /> } />
    <Route path="/:slug"          element={ <Layout postType="landing-page" /> } />
  </Routes>
</BrowserRouter>

A single-segment URL is assumed to be a landing page; two segments are read as post type and slug. This mirrors the PHP rewrite rules, where landing pages are rewritten to the site root.

Render chain

Component tree 
index.tsx  (BrowserRouter)
└── Layout.tsx                    Header + Footer + ErrorBoundary + loading gate
      └── TemplateLoader          fetches the post, picks a template by REST slug
            ├── LandingPage       panel-driven pages
            │     └── Panel       reads page_panel_type_{N}
            │           └── PanelLoader   lazy-loads the panel component
            ├── SimplePage        prose pages
            ├── Form              standalone form pages
            └── Page404           fallback

Layout

Layout.tsx owns the page frame and three pieces of cross-cutting behaviour:

  • Loading gate — a Loading overlay is shown until the template reports it has rendered, with a one-second minimum so fast transitions do not flash. The footer is withheld until then, preventing it from jumping up under a half-built page.
  • Error boundary — keyed to pathname + search, so navigating away from a crashed route recovers automatically.
  • Layout classes — templates call back with a class list that lands on <main id="content">, giving CSS a hook for the post type and page slug.

An iframe mode renders the template bare — no header, footer or back-to-top — for embedding. PHP supports it through an iframe/{slug} rewrite rule.

TemplateLoader

Fetches the post, then selects a component from a map keyed by REST slug: form, landing-page, simple-page, and 404 as the fallback. Two aliases are applied first — media becomes media-library and page becomes simple-page. Extension templates are merged in from /extensions/app/components/templates/single/*.tsx; a core key always wins a collision.

Panels

LandingPage reads {prefix}_panel_count and renders that many <Panel> components, numbered from 1. Each Panel:

  1. Reads {prefix}_hide_panel_{N} and bails out if the panel is hidden.
  2. Reads {prefix}_panel_type_{N} to decide what to render.
  3. Assembles a class list — panel, panel-type-{type}, plus alignment, overlay, alternation and every class panelClasses() derives from the background field.
  4. Computes an anchor ID from the explicit ID field, falling back to a slugified title, then the panel type.
  5. Renders through PanelWrapper — or inside a Modal, if it is a form panel with Modal checked.

Panel components are lazy-loaded, so a page ships only the panel code it uses.

Partial templates

PartialTemplateLoader renders individual post cards inside panels. It selects a view type — block or simple — then a component within that view by post type, falling back to the default. Add templates.block['devo_case_study'] to give one post type a bespoke card without affecting the rest.

State

useMenus
Fetches all menu locations once and caches them on window.menus. Concurrent callers share a single in-flight promise, so a header and footer mounting together produce one request, not two. Also holds mobile menu open/closed state.
useCurrentPage
The active page slug, so components deep in the tree can react to it without prop drilling.
useLandingPage
Present but not wired into the render path.

Hooks

useCountUp animates a number when it scrolls into view (used by the stats panel); useScrollReveal attaches intersection-observer reveal behaviour.

Alternating layouts

Setting Media Alignment to alternate on a text-media panel makes Panel add an even or odd class based on the panel's index, so consecutive panels flip sides automatically.

Custom tags in editor content

parse() is what lets shortcodes cross the PHP/React boundary. functions.display.php renders shortcodes into pseudo-tags such as <CTA url="…" text="…" />, which wp_kses is configured to permit, and parse() converts into real React components on the client. Editors get working buttons and images inside rich text without any HTML leaking through.

SCSS throughout, using the modern @use module system. Component styles are imported directly inside the React component that needs them, so Vite code-splits CSS alongside the component chunk.

The separation that matters

Framework vs. theme

Styles under app/styles/ are structural and layout only — no brand colours, backgrounds or shadows. All visual identity lives in extensions/app/styles/. This is what lets one framework serve differently-branded sites, and it is the rule most likely to be broken accidentally. If you find yourself adding a colour to app/styles/, it belongs in the extensions layer.

Core abstracts

FileProvides
_color.scssBase values, all HSL
_breakpoint.scssmax-320 … max-1300 mixins, plus print
_size.scssRadii, padding, margins, shadows, header and admin-bar heights
_block.scssblock-one … block-four grid mixins that degrade responsively
_font.scss, _function.scss, _mixin.scssType stack, colour functions, shared mixins

Import them as a bundle: @use '@/styles/abstracts' as *;

Class naming

BEM — .block__element--modifier. Every selector carries its element (ul.blocks, li.blocks__item) unless the class is deliberately open-ended about its tag, such as .blocks__link, which may render as an <a>, a <span> or a router <Link>.

The extensions theming layer

The shipped example is a dark “deep-field” astronomy theme. It demonstrates the pattern any site theme should follow.

Tokens as custom properties. abstracts/_tokens.scss defines the palette on :root as CSS custom properties — surfaces, text, a single accent hue, line colours, type stacks and metrics — so the palette can be re-pointed without recompiling. Breakpoints must resolve at build time, so those stay SCSS variables.

Type roles, not ad-hoc sizes. abstracts/_type.scss exposes mixins named for their role — display(), body-copy(), mono(), mono-label(), eyebrow — so a size change happens once rather than across seventeen partials.

Fonts are self-hosted. Instrument Serif, Hanken Grotesk and JetBrains Mono ship as woff2 in extensions/app/styles/fonts/, subset for latin and latin-ext, with the variable faces covering every weight in one file. No render-blocking third-party requests.

Why every rule is nested under #root

extensions-global.css is enqueued after devo-global.css, but per-component stylesheets are code-split by Vite and injected into <head> at runtime when their chunk loads — landing after the extensions layer and winning every specificity tie. Scoping to #root, the element React mounts into and therefore an ancestor of everything it renders, adds one ID to each selector, which beats any class-only rule regardless of source order.

Rules that must sit outside the app root — :root tokens, @font-face, html/body, keyframes — live in abstracts/ and base/ instead.

Per-page stylesheets

A landing page's CSS admin field names a stylesheet in app/styles/pages/, which LandingPage.tsx dynamically imports at runtime. Failures are swallowed, so a stale value degrades to no extra styling rather than a crash.

Server-rendered meta

header.php resolves the post before React exists and emits the crawler-critical tags: title, canonical, the Open Graph set, Twitter card, description, robots directive and JSON-LD. If no post object is available it falls back to looking one up by request path, defaulting to home.

Which field feeds which tag is declared per post type in the seo setting, and supports fallback chains:

php 
'seo' => [
    'title'       => 'SEO Title||post_title',  // SEO Title, else the post title
    'image'       => 'SEO Image||Media',      // SEO Image, else the panel media
    'description' => 'SEO Description',
],

The tags carry data-react-helmet="true" so the client-side SEOTags component can take ownership of them on navigation without duplicating them.

Robots

devo_noindex() applies the devo_noindex filter and returns noindex or index, follow. The shipped rule forces noindex for tags, attachments, native pages, and every request on dev or stg. For individual posts it honours the post's own noindex and hide_post fields. Core sitemaps are disabled.

Structured data

Schema is declared per post type: '@type' is a literal, and every other key maps a schema.org property to a field label. Landing pages let editors override the type per page — WebPage, AboutPage, ContactPage or SearchResultsPage — from the Admin box. devo_get_schema() assembles the object server-side; StructuredData.tsx re-emits it on client navigation.

Analytics and cookie consent

  1. Production onlyGTM markup is emitted solely when DO_ENVIRONMENT is prod.
  2. Consent requiredPHP includes the GTM snippet only if the devo_cookie_consent cookie equals accepted.
  3. Accept in-pageCookieConsent.tsx sets the cookie and injects GTM immediately, with no reload.

Consent banner copy is editable in Site Settings, so it can be revised without a deploy. The container ID is defined once as DO_GTM_ID in functions.php and passed to React as window.devoGTM.

Per-site configuration

Three values are currently hard-coded in the theme and must be changed when it is deployed for a different site: DO_GTM_ID and the Google site-verification token in header.php, and the login-screen title returned by devo_login_url_title(). That function is wrapped in function_exists(), so a child theme can override it cleanly.

Cache busting

Stylesheets are versioned with DO_VER:

php · functions.php, line 3 
define( 'DO_VER', DO_ENVIRONMENT == 'local' ? time() : 'DEPLOY_TIMESTAMP' );

Locally this is time(), so nothing is ever cached while you work. On every other environment the literal string DEPLOY_TIMESTAMP is a placeholder your deployment pipeline is expected to replace with a real stamp. If the pipeline does not perform that substitution, the version string never changes and browsers serve stale CSS after a deploy. JavaScript is unaffected — it is content-hashed by Vite and resolved through the manifest.

Deployment checklist

  1. Run npm run build. TypeScript must pass.
  2. Commit public/dist/ — the build output is versioned, and the theme cannot enqueue anything without the manifest.
  3. Confirm DO_ENVIRONMENT is correct for the target.
  4. Confirm the pipeline substitutes DEPLOY_TIMESTAMP.
  5. Flush permalinks after any change to a post type slug, rewrite rule or archive setting.
Rewrite rules

Landing pages save with a manually-constructed guid and flush rewrite rules on every save, because their slugs live at the site root and collisions with other routes are otherwise silent. If a page 404s after a slug change, flushing permalinks is the first thing to try.

Git attributes

.gitattributes marks *.map, *.css, *.svg and everything under public/dist/ as -diff, keeping generated output out of code review.

Where to look first

Page renders blank
Check the browser console for the getPost URL logged in non-production, then open that URL directly. Usually a slug mismatch or a post type whose rest_slug has no matching template.
Panel selectable but empty
The devo_panel_types value does not match the kebab-case key derived from the component filename.
Styles missing after deploy
DEPLOY_TIMESTAMP was not substituted, or the partial is not @used.
Two React roots / app crashes
Something added a ?ver= query to the entry script tag.
404 after a slug change
Flush permalinks.
